docs.text: Crops are central master data. They are assigned to fields and selected during application documentation. This allows PSMSimple to show matching fields and store the BBCH code with the application.

docs.title: Create a new crop
docs.text:
1. Open Crops.
  2. Click + New Crop.
  3. Enter the name.
  4. Enter the EPPO code.
  5. Save the crop.

The EPPO code provides a clear technical assignment. Use the official crop code whenever possible.

docs.title: Maintain BBCH codes
docs.text:
BBCH codes can be maintained for saved crops.

  1. Open a crop with Edit.
  2. Click + Add BBCH.
  3. Enter the code, label, and optionally a description.
  4. Optionally add a sorting value.
  5. Save the BBCH entry.

The sorting value controls the display order of BBCH codes. Often it makes sense to use the BBCH code itself as the sorting value.

docs.title: Edit or delete a crop
docs.text:
Use Edit to change the name, EPPO code, and BBCH codes. Use Delete to remove a crop.

Delete crops carefully. If fields or applications depend on them, first check whether the crop is still in use.

docs.title: Add BBCH is disabled
docs.text: Save the crop first. BBCH codes can only be assigned meaningfully to an already saved crop.

docs.title: BBCH code does not appear during documentation
docs.text: Check whether the BBCH code was saved for the correct crop. Open the crop with Edit and review the BBCH table.

docs.title: Crop does not appear for a field
docs.text: Check whether the crop was saved. Afterwards, you can assign it to a field in Fields.

docs.title: At a Glance
docs.text:
In Inventory, you see current stock levels for plant protection products and record incoming or outgoing movements. Warning and minimum stock levels come from product master data or inventory defaults.

Important features:

  • overview of all product stock levels
  • status OK, warning, critical, or negative
  • movements for purchase, correction, and disposal
  • movement history with date, type, quantity, and note

docs.title: Prerequisite
docs.text: For a product to appear in inventory, it must exist in Plant Protection Products. There you can also maintain inventory unit, minimum stock level, and warning stock level.

docs.title: Open overview
docs.text:
Open Inventory. In Overview, you see each plant protection product with current stock and unit.

The status shows whether the stock level is normal or should be checked:

  • OK: stock is within the normal range
  • Warning: stock is below the warning level
  • Critical: stock is below the minimum level
  • Negative: stock is calculated below zero

docs.title: Create a movement
docs.text:
1. Open the desired product in the overview.
  2. Click + Movement.
  3. Select the movement type.
  4. Enter quantity and date.
  5. Optionally add a note.
  6. Click Book.

Available movement types:

  • Purchase for incoming stock
  • Correction + for later increases
  • Correction - for later decreases
  • Disposal for outgoing stock

Applications may also appear automatically as inventory movements when they are saved.

docs.title: Use movement history
docs.text:
In Movement History, you see recent movements. Use Number of entries to show 50, 200, or 500 entries.

The table shows:

  • date
  • product
  • type
  • quantity
  • note
  • source

docs.title: A product is missing from inventory
docs.text: Check whether the product is saved in Plant Protection Products.

docs.title: Stock is negative
docs.text: Check the movement history. Often a purchase or correction is missing, or an application was documented with too high a quantity.

docs.title: Movement cannot be created
docs.text: If + Movement is not visible, you probably do not have write permissions.

docs.title: At a Glance
docs.text:
In Reports, you record observations, damage, tasks, or notes related to fields. Reports can be filtered by status, type, and field. A report can include photos, coordinates, priority, and processing status.

Typical details:

  • date
  • field
  • type
  • priority
  • status
  • title and description
  • coordinates
  • photos

docs.title: Open reports
docs.text: Open Reports. Filters are shown on the left, the report list in the middle, and details or the form on the right.

docs.title: Filter reports
docs.text:
You can filter reports by:

  • Status, such as open, in progress, done, or discarded
  • Type, such as wildlife damage, hail damage, disease, or pest
  • Field

The list updates after a filter changes.

docs.title: Create a new report
docs.text:
1. Click + New Report.
  2. Select date, field, type, priority, and status.
  3. Enter a short title.
  4. Add a description.
  5. Check or add coordinates.
  6. Add photos if needed.
  7. Click Save.

Date, type, and title are especially important so the report can be found later.

docs.title: Add photos
docs.text:
You can select images from the gallery or, if supported by the device, take a photo directly.

Photos are useful for:

  • damage to vines, posts, or wire
  • disease symptoms
  • pest infestation
  • hail or wildlife damage
  • other field observations

docs.title: Edit a report
docs.text: Select a report and click Edit. Change the required details and save the report again.

docs.title: Complete a report
docs.text: Set the status to Done when the report has been handled. Use Discarded for entries that are no longer relevant.

docs.title: No reports are visible
docs.text: Check the filters. A selected status, type, or field may return no results.

docs.title: Camera is not available
docs.text: Camera availability depends on device, browser, and permissions. Use Select gallery instead.

docs.title: Report cannot be edited
docs.text: If edit or delete actions are not visible, you probably do not have write permissions.

docs.title: At a Glance
docs.text:
In Plant Protection Products, you maintain products that are later used in applications. If possible, select a product from the search so the approval number and active substances are filled automatically. Add the application rate unit, bee hazard classification, and inventory details.

Important fields:

  • name
  • approval number
  • active substances
  • application rate unit
  • bee hazard classification
  • inventory unit
  • minimum and warning stock level

docs.title: What plant protection products are used for
docs.text: Plant protection products are selected during application documentation and recorded with an application rate. Master data helps identify products clearly and avoids entering recurring information again and again.

docs.title: Create a new product
docs.text:
1. Open Plant Protection Products.
  2. Click + New Product.
  3. Enter the name.
  4. If possible, select a result from the search.
  5. Add the remaining details.
  6. Click Save.

docs.title: Use search
docs.text:
While entering the name, PSMSimple shows matching results. When you select a result, the approval number and active substances can be filled automatically.

If no result appears, check the spelling or create the product manually.

docs.title: Application rate unit
docs.text:
The unit is later shown next to the entered application rate in the documentation.

Typical units are:

  • kg/ha
  • l/ha
  • g/ha
  • ml/ha

docs.title: Bee hazard classification
docs.text:
Select the matching classification:

  • B1
  • B2
  • B3
  • B4

The classification serves as an important note in the master data. Always verify legally relevant information against the current approval and product information.

docs.title: Inventory details
docs.text:
If you use inventory management, also maintain:

  • inventory unit
  • minimum stock level
  • warning stock level

These details support stock warnings and later inventory management.

docs.title: Edit or delete a product
docs.text:
Use Edit to change existing products. Use Delete to remove a product from the master data list.

Only delete products if they are no longer needed. Historical applications keep the stored data.

docs.title: Product does not appear in documentation
docs.text: Check whether the product was saved. Then reopen the documentation page or reload the application.

docs.title: Approval number or active substances cannot be edited
docs.text: These fields may be filled automatically and protected through search selection. Select the matching search result or create the product with the available details.

docs.title: Wrong unit in documentation
docs.text: Edit the product and correct the application rate unit. New applications will then use the updated unit.

docs.title: At a Glance
docs.text:
Forecast calculates suitable spray windows for selected sites. PSMSimple evaluates weather data using configured thresholds such as wind, precipitation, temperature, humidity, and drying time.

You select:

  • sites
  • time range
  • minimum window duration

PSMSimple then shows the best time window and alternatives.

docs.title: Prerequisite
docs.text: For a forecast, sites with coordinates must exist. Without sites or coordinates, PSMSimple cannot retrieve weather data for the correct location.

docs.title: Open forecast
docs.text: Open Forecast. You will see the settings and the result area.

docs.title: Select sites
docs.text:
Select one or more sites. Use All to select all sites and None to clear the selection.

If no sites are shown, create sites or fields with coordinates first.

docs.title: Set time range
docs.text:
Select the time range for the calculation:

  • today
  • until tomorrow
  • next 2 days
  • next 3 days
  • next 4 days
  • next 5 days

The default range can be changed in Settings.

docs.title: Set minimum duration
docs.text: Minimum window duration defines how long a suitable time window must be. For example, a value of 2 hours means shorter windows are not accepted as results.

docs.title: Calculate forecast
docs.text:
Click Calculate forecast. PSMSimple loads weather data and evaluates time windows using the configured thresholds.

The result shows:

  • best time window across all selected sites
  • site
  • duration
  • score
  • start time
  • additional windows and alternatives

docs.title: Understand thresholds
docs.text:
Thresholds are maintained in Settings. They include:

  • maximum wind
  • maximum precipitation
  • minimum and maximum temperature
  • minimum humidity
  • drying time after application
  • earliest and latest hour

The forecast is a decision aid. Always check technical and legal requirements before the actual application.

docs.title: No suitable time window found
docs.text: The current weather conditions do not meet the thresholds. Check alternatives, extend the time range, or review the defaults in settings.

docs.title: Sites cannot be loaded
docs.text: Check whether sites exist and whether the server connection works.

docs.title: Result looks unexpected
docs.text: Check the site coordinates and the thresholds in settings.
